$comment: Symptom-first help: what to do, in order, when the owner starts from what the car does rather than from a code. Each step points at an existing test, chain, guide, check or page ('quick-test', 'drain-finder', 'ghost-hunter'); tests fail if an id doesn't exist. Our own words; nothing here is a specification.

symptoms.title: Won't start, or won't crank
symptoms.summary: Start with what the car recorded during the failed start, then the battery.

steps.why: Read every module first: a failed start usually leaves faults in the engine computer or the key module.
Checks battery voltage, whether the engine is turning, and the faults logged during the failed start. Read-only.
If it cranks slowly or just clicks: tells a tired battery from a charging problem.
If the steering lock symbol is on and nothing happens when you press Start.
If the dash stays dark or modules don't answer at all.

symptoms.title: Rough idle, shaking or stalling
symptoms.summary: Find out whether it's one cylinder, the mixture, or the idle control, before buying parts.

steps.why: Watches how steady the idle is with the air conditioning off and on, each cylinder and the mixture.
Compares the cylinders: one that stands out points at its coil, plug or injector.
Shows whether the engine is correcting a lean or rich mixture.
If the trims are lean at idle: narrows down a vacuum leak.
What to swap and check when one cylinder misfires.
Test a coil by swapping it before buying one.

symptoms.title: Check engine light, or poor fuel economy
symptoms.summary: Most engine lights on these cars come down to mixture, misfires, VANOS or an oxygen sensor.

steps.why: Read the engine computer's faults: the code decides which path below applies.
For lean or rich codes: what the correction pattern points to.
For lean codes: narrows down a vacuum leak.
Step-by-step checks for lean and rich mixture.
For camshaft timing codes: target against actual position.
For oxygen sensor heater codes.
For secondary air codes after a cold start.

symptoms.title: Misfire, or a flashing engine light
symptoms.summary: A flashing engine light means misfires that can damage the catalytic converter: don't keep driving hard.

steps.why: Shows which cylinder is weak, even before a misfire fault is stored.
Coil, plug, injector and leak checks in order.
Swap the coil to another cylinder and see if the misfire follows it.
Misfires on several cylinders with lean trims point at a leak or fuel delivery, not at coils.

symptoms.title: Loss of power, or limp mode
symptoms.summary: The engine computer cuts power to protect the engine. The stored fault says which system it's unhappy with.

steps.why: Read the faults first: limp mode always leaves one.
Turbo engines: boost leaks, wastegates and the charge pipe.
Direct-injection engines: fuel pressure under load.
Camshaft timing that can't reach its target costs power.
Running short of fuel at 2,500 rpm points at fuel delivery or the air-mass meter.

symptoms.title: Overheating, or a temperature warning
symptoms.summary: Stop and let it cool before testing. Never open the expansion tank cap on a hot engine.

steps.why: Read the engine computer: water pump and thermostat faults are stored there.
What to check, in order, on engines with an electric water pump and a map-controlled thermostat.
Engines with an electric water pump: the speed asked for against the speed the pump reports.
Check the pump's connector and supply before replacing it.
After topping up or replacing parts: the bleed routine, watched by Klemme15.

symptoms.title: Battery goes flat when the car sits
symptoms.summary: Something keeps the car awake, or the battery is worn out. The car records clues about both.

steps.why: Battery going flat? on the Faults page: the car's own clues, then a step-by-step hunt for the circuit.
Rules out a battery that isn't being charged properly.
How to measure the parked current and find the circuit.
A known cause: wires that crack in the trunk lid or tailgate harness.

symptoms.title: Battery or charging warning while driving
symptoms.summary: Check the charging voltage before replacing the battery.

steps.why: Measures resting, idle and loaded voltage, and says what the pattern points to.
Alternator, battery sensor and cables, in order.
A bad ground strap looks like a bad alternator.

symptoms.title: ABS, DSC or traction control light
symptoms.summary: Usually one wheel speed sensor or the steering angle sensor. The fault names the corner.

steps.why: Read the stability control module: the fault says which sensor.
Wheel speed sensor faults: sensor, wiring and the ring it reads.
Measure the sensor before buying one.
Steering angle faults, usually after an alignment or a steering repair.

symptoms.title: Airbag light
symptoms.summary: Reading the fault is safe. Repairs on the airbag system belong with a qualified mechanic: an airbag can fire during work on its wiring.

steps.why: Read the airbag module's fault: it names the circuit.
What seat, belt and airbag circuit faults mean, and what's safe to check yourself.

symptoms.title: Lights, windows or mirrors stopped working
symptoms.summary: These share one module on many cars, so check it and its power before the individual parts.

steps.why: See whether the footwell module answers and what it stored.
If the footwell module doesn't answer and several lights and windows died at once.
Fuses and power supplies for the body modules.
Trunk release, number plate lights or reverse lights acting up.

symptoms.title: Steering lock warning, or the car won't switch on
symptoms.summary: When the electric steering lock fails or loses power, the car can refuse to start and show a steering lock message.

steps.why: Read the key module's faults.
What the warning means, what to check, and the counter reset.

symptoms.title: A problem that comes and goes
symptoms.summary: Catch it when it happens instead of guessing afterwards.

steps.why: The Ghost Hunter watches the engine while you drive and saves the minute before and after the moment it happens.
Intermittent faults are very often a connector: how to check one properly.
A poor ground gives faults that come and go: how to test one.

symptoms.title: Many warnings at once
symptoms.summary: Several systems complaining together almost always share one cause: voltage, or one module the others depend on.

steps.why: The Faults page groups faults that share a cause: look for "Likely one cause, not many".
A weak battery or charging fault is the most common cause.
When modules report missing messages from each other.
Power supplies and fuses shared by several modules.
